name: Lake Mansour Eddahbi
hero_subtitle: Reservoir landscape — birds, shoreline and a change of scene from mud-brick villages.

overview.title: Water on the Desert Edge
overview.p1: Lake Mansour Eddahbi is the reservoir that holds water for the region and offers Ouarzazate a different horizon: open water, birds in season, and shoreline walks instead of kasbah stairs. It is not a swimming resort; it is a landscape stop when you need a break from earthen walls.
overview.p2: A short visit works at the end of a town day or before a longer transfer. Bring binoculars if you care about birds; bring a wind layer if the afternoon breeze picks up.
overview.p3: Access points vary — a driver who knows a quiet shore is more useful than a random pull-off.

q1.question: Can I swim?
q1.answer: Not a beach resort — treat it as a viewpoint and walk, follow local practice.

q2.question: How far?
q2.answer: Close to Ouarzazate — a short drive depending on the access point.

q3.question: Best season?
q3.answer: Cooler months are more pleasant; bird activity varies by season.

q4.question: Do I need a guide at Lake Mansour Eddahbi?
q4.answer: Optional for a simple visit; useful for history and safe paths on fragile mud brick.

q5.question: Is Lake Mansour Eddahbi suitable for families?
q5.answer: Yes with supervision on steps, rooftops and uneven ground.

food.title: Picnic or return to town
food.p1: Limited facilities on the shore. Pack water and a simple snack, or eat in Ouarzazate.
food.p2: This is a landscape stop, not a dining destination.
food.li2: Simple picnic if you have shade
food.li3: Lunch in town before or after

tips.title: Practical Tips for Visiting Lake Mansour Eddahbi

1.title: Access
1.desc: Ask your hotel or driver for a current quiet shoreline — not every pull-off is equal.

2.title: Wind
2.desc: Afternoons can be breezy on the open water — a light layer helps.

3.title: Birds
3.desc: Early morning is better for wildlife; midday is for the view only.
